bug_description.normalized: The staged 33702-byte witness reaches the vulnerable fuzz-only path in commit `3289a66db7145c081ff1d5fa987f0cfec0563dc5`. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` truncates that file to the first 32768 bytes and copies them into global `static_data[32768]`, filling the array completely. `config_open_for_fuzzing()` still passes the full copied length to `config_init_data()`, so the lexer state is initialized with `end = static_data + 32768`, one byte past the array. Direct inspection of the copied prefix shows no `\0`, `=`, `#`, or `$`; the only whitespace is two ASCII spaces at offsets 10047 and 24944, so after the last space `lex_config()` dispatches a final 7823-byte token to `lex_string()`, and that suffix contains no `${` sequence that would divert into `lex_variable`. `lex_string()` consumes that suffix until `next()` hits `lexer->end`, at which point `next()` sets `pos = end + 1` and returns `\0`; the unconditional `backup()` then decrements to `end` and dereferences `*lexer->pos` at `static_data + 32768`, producing the saved AddressSanitizer `global-buffer-overflow READ 1` at `src/lib/lwan-config.c:279`. The fix expresses the missing fuzz-only obligation by changing `config_open_for_fuzzing()` to call `config_init_data(config, data, len - 1)`, reserving one in-bounds byte for this EOF/backup path, but Stage 02 did not dynamically validate the fixed image.

source.description: First non-harness parser state initialization that materializes the copied fuzz buffer and its extent into lexer state. For the saved witness, `pos` and `start` begin at `static_data` and `end` becomes `static_data + 32768`, the one-past-array address that later feeds the EOF/backup bug.
source.value_from: The staged file `gt_results/arvo_18447/poc` is exactly 33702 bytes (sha256 `36b6551e6e14ef121974a9da1a98b5c760f61dbbaeffbd784676a0a0e4d052f6`). `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` truncates it to `size = 32768` and copies only the first 32768 bytes into `static_data`. In that copied prefix there is no `\0`, `=`, `#`, or `$`; the only whitespace is two ASCII space bytes at offsets 10047 and 24944. The final 7823-byte suffix from offset 24945 through 32767 therefore reaches the end of the copied array and contains no `${` sequence that would divert `lex_string()` into `lex_variable`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan crash site. After `next()` has already moved `lexer->pos` to `lexer->end + 1`, `backup()` decrements it once and dereferences `*lexer->pos` at `static_data + 32768`, the first byte to the right of the 32768-byte global array.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `backup /src/lwan/src/lib/lwan-config.c:279:9` and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of global variable `static_data` defined in `src/bin/fuzz/config_fuzzer.cc:44` with size 32768.

root_cause.description: Fuzz-only extent bug. `config_open_for_fuzzing()` passes the full copied length into the lexer initializer, so when the harness fills all 32768 bytes of `static_data` the lexer gets no in-bounds slack byte for EOF handling and later `backup()` inspection.
root_cause.note: The fix changes this exact call to `config_init_data(config, data, len - 1)`, reserving one byte inside `static_data` for the EOF/backup path instead of letting `end` land just past the array.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant witness state is the fuzz helper's exact copied extent. For the saved 33702-byte file, the harness truncates `size` to 32768 and overwrites every byte of global `static_data[0..32767]`, leaving no additional in-bounds byte beyond the parsed data.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Saved witness length 33702; clamped parser-visible length 32768; copied prefix sha256 `2b532a39fac056d1f3acc2f345aee2a1b2364cdaa7833db68c254e35b29ece00`.

parser_admitted.description: After earlier space-delimited tokens, `lex_config()` reaches the final delimiter at copied offset 24944, skips it as whitespace, then sees `'V'` at offset 24945. Because that byte is not `$` and still satisfies `isstring(chr)`, control enters `lex_string()` for the last token that runs to EOF.

fine_trace.note: The staged witness file is 33702 bytes, so the fuzz helper clamps `size` to `sizeof(static_data) == 32768` before parsing. That exact clamp makes the later copy fill the entire global array instead of leaving a spare byte inside it.

Copies the first 32768 bytes of the witness into `static_data[0..32767]`. Because `size` now equals the array size, every byte in the global object becomes attacker-controlled and there is no unread copied byte left inside the array after offset 32767.

Root cause. The fuzz-only entry point forwards the fully occupied buffer and the full copied length `32768` into `config_init_data()` unchanged. The later fix changes only this handoff to `len - 1`, showing that this path must reserve one in-bounds byte for the lexer's EOF/backup behavior.

Source. This is the first non-harness parser statement that materializes the copied bytes and their extent into lexer state. For the saved run, `pos = start = static_data` and `end = static_data + 32768`, the one-past-array address that later becomes readable only if a spare in-bounds byte exists.

After earlier space-delimited tokens, the last non-string delimiter in the copied prefix is the space byte at offset 24944. The next byte at offset 24945 is `'V'`, not `$`, so the `${` variable branch at lines 455-456 is false and `isstring(chr)` is true; `lex_config()` dispatches the trailing suffix into `lex_string()` instead of `lex_variable` or a delimiter path.

The final token begins at copied offset 24945 and runs through offset 32767. Direct inspection of those 7823 bytes shows no whitespace, `=`, `#`, `\0`, `$`, or `${`, so the variable-handling branch never triggers, every copied byte in that suffix keeps `isstring(chr)` true, and `lex_string()` continues until `next()` finally reports EOF after the last copied byte.

Once step 5 has consumed the byte at offset 32767, the next `next()` call arrives with `lexer->pos == lexer->end == static_data + 32768`. This EOF branch therefore advances `lexer->pos` to `static_data + 32769` and returns `\0` to terminate `lex_string()`.

After step 6 returns `\0`, `lex_string()` exits its loop and unconditionally calls `backup(lexer)` at line 317. This statement moves `lexer->pos` from `static_data + 32769` back to `static_data + 32768`, the first byte past the array rather than the last byte inside it.

Sink. `backup()` immediately dereferences the pointer from step 7, so it reads 1 byte at `static_data + 32768`, just past the last valid element `static_data[32767]`. This matches the saved ASan `global-buffer-overflow READ 1` in `backup` with stack `backup -> lex_string -> lex_next`.

allocation_context.note: ASan identifies the faulting address as 0 bytes to the right of global variable `static_data` defined here with size 32768.

format.name: Exact overlong config-fuzzer witness whose truncated copied prefix ends with an unterminated string token
format.contract: Exactly the 33702-byte witness stored in `gt_results/arvo_18447/poc` (sha256 `36b6551e6e14ef121974a9da1a98b5c760f61dbbaeffbd784676a0a0e4d052f6`). `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` truncates it to the first 32768 bytes before parsing. In that copied prefix there is no `\0`, `=`, `#`, or `$`; the only whitespace is two ASCII space bytes at offsets 10047 and 24944, so after the last space `lex_config()` starts a final string token at offset 24945. The trailing 7823-byte suffix from offsets 24945 through 32767 also contains no `${` sequence, and every copied byte in that suffix still satisfies `isstring(chr)`. Those exact witness properties make `lex_string()` run to EOF, after which `next()` places `lexer->pos` at `static_data + 32769` and `backup()` reads `*` at `static_data + 32768`, the first byte past the 32768-byte global array. Stage 02 does not generalize beyond this saved witness.
